title: Best Apps to Practice Speaking a Language in 2026 (16 Apps)
summary: 16 apps for speaking practice compared: AI tutors, human tutors, language exchange and audio courses. Prices, free options, platforms and who each app suits.
body_markdown:
*Updated November 2026 · Prices and ratings checked October 2026 (US)*


## The short answer


**For most learners, ISSEN is the best app for practising speaking a language.** It is a realtime AI voice tutor: you have open-ended spoken conversations with a tutor that has its own voice and personality, it corrects you as you go, and it remembers earlier sessions, so each conversation builds on the last. It runs on the web, iOS and Android.


Other apps you'll see compared, and what each one is actually for:


- **Speak:** a structured AI course with speaking drills and AI conversation, for learners who want a lesson path.
- **italki:** human tutors you book and pay per lesson.
- **HelloTalk:** free language exchange with native speakers.
- **Tandem:** free language exchange in 300+ languages, including sign languages.
- **Praktika:** conversations with AI avatar tutors.
- **Talkpal:** an AI tutor with a free daily allowance, in 130+ languages.
- **Langua:** AI conversation with natural voices and detailed feedback afterwards.
- **ELSA Speak:** English pronunciation coaching.
- **Pimsleur:** recorded audio lessons, for practising hands-free.
- **Fluently, Talkio AI, LinguaLive, OGIMA, Linguino and TalkHabit:** AI tutors and structured role-play with a narrower focus, covered below.

## How we compared them


We looked only at what helps you speak:


1. **Speaking time.** How much of a session you spend talking out loud, not tapping or reading.
2. **Who you talk to.** An AI tutor, a paid human tutor, or a volunteer native speaker.
3. **Feedback.** Whether you get corrected, on what (grammar, pronunciation, word choice), and how.
4. **Freedom.** Scripted exercises versus open conversation on topics you choose.
5. **Cost of real practice.** What it costs to practice daily, not just to sign up.
6. **Platforms and languages.**


## The apps


### 1. ISSEN — an AI voice tutor for practising speaking a language


ISSEN is a realtime AI voice tutor for speaking practice through open-ended conversations. You pick a tutor (each has its own voice and personality) and talk about whatever you like; it corrects you as you go and remembers earlier sessions, so the next conversation builds on the last. It also has in-context flashcards from your own conversations and a shadowing mode for pronunciation. 4.7 stars on the App Store, 4.6 on Google Play; backed by Y Combinator.


- **Who it suits:** learners past the basics who want lots of unscripted speaking time
- **Free option:** 5 minutes of conversation
- **Price:** USD 10–29/month, depending on plan and country
- **Platforms:** web, iOS, Android
- **Note:** most useful once you can hold a basic conversation.


### 2. Speak — a structured course plus AI conversation


Speak combines a structured course with open-ended speaking practice against an AI tutor. Lessons get you saying full sentences out loud from the first day, and its AI tutor gives feedback on pronunciation, phrasing and grammar. It is one of the most-rated apps in the category (4.8 on the App Store from 65,000+ ratings).


- **Who it suits:** learners who want a clear path and lots of guided speaking reps
- **Free option:** 7-day trial
- **Price:** $17.99/month or $83.99/year (Premium, US App Store); varies by region
- **Platforms:** iOS, Android
- **Note:** six target languages for English speakers, and no free tier after the 7-day trial.


### 3. italki — human tutors you book per lesson


italki is a marketplace of independent tutors for 150+ languages. You book one-to-one video lessons, so you get a real person who can follow your interests and correct you in context.


- **Who it suits:** learners who want human feedback and can schedule lessons
- **Free option:** free to sign up; trial lessons are cheap
- **Price:** each tutor sets their own rate per lesson; italki Plus is $5.99/month
- **Platforms:** web, iOS, Android
- **Note:** lessons are booked and paid one at a time, at each tutor's own rate.


### 4. HelloTalk — free language exchange with native speakers


HelloTalk is a language exchange: you chat, voice-message and call native speakers who are learning your language. It's free, and it's the most social option here.


- **Who it suits:** intermediate learners who want real people and real slang, for free
- **Free option:** yes; VIP is optional
- **Price:** VIP $12.99/month or $79.99/year (US App Store)
- **Platforms:** iOS, Android
- **Note:** practice depends on finding a partner, and the useful tools sit behind VIP.


### 5. Tandem — free exchange in 300+ languages


Tandem works like HelloTalk: you find native speakers and practise by text, voice and video. It covers 300+ languages, including sign languages, the widest list here.


- **Who it suits:** learners who want a partner for a less common language
- **Free option:** yes; Pro is optional
- **Platforms:** web, iOS, Android
- **Note:** new accounts are reviewed before you can join.


### 6. Praktika — AI avatar conversations


Praktika puts you in video-style conversations with AI avatar tutors in 14 languages. It's popular (4.8 on the App Store, 1M+ ratings on Google Play) and good for learners who find talking to a "face" more natural than talking to a voice.


- **Who it suits:** shy speakers who want a friendly, structured warm-up
- **Free option:** limited free plan
- **Price:** from about $8/month on annual plans; App Store prices vary with promotions
- **Platforms:** iOS, Android
- **Note:** iOS and Android only, and the free plan covers three avatars.


### 7. Talkpal — AI conversation with a free daily allowance


Talkpal is an AI tutor covering 130+ languages, with open conversation and role-play practice on web and mobile. The free tier gives 10 minutes a day, which is enough for a daily habit.


- **Who it suits:** budget learners and less common languages
- **Free option:** 10 minutes/day, plus a 14-day trial of Premium
- **Price:** $19.99/month or $119.99/year (US App Store)
- **Platforms:** web, iOS, Android
- **Note:** the free tier is 10 minutes a day.


### 8. Langua — AI conversation with natural voices


Langua (from LanguaTalk) is an AI conversation partner in 23 languages, with natural-sounding voices, a choice of dialects, a real-time call mode and detailed feedback after each conversation. LanguaTalk also offers human tutors if you want both.


- **Who it suits:** intermediate learners who want realistic conversation and detailed corrections
- **Free option:** 3 call-minutes a day
- **Price:** $19.99/month Standard; $29.99/month Unlimited (US App Store)
- **Platforms:** web, iOS, Android
- **Note:** the free tier is 3 call-minutes a day.


### 9. ELSA Speak — English pronunciation coaching


ELSA scores your English pronunciation sound by sound and drills what you get wrong. It is English only, but nothing here is more precise for accent work.


- **Who it suits:** English learners working on accent and clarity
- **Free option:** free tier and 7-day trial
- **Price:** $19.99/month; about $99.99/year (US App Store; promotions common)
- **Platforms:** iOS, Android
- **Note:** English only.


### 10. Pimsleur — audio lessons for hands-free practice


Pimsleur's audio lessons prompt you to answer out loud, hands-free, in 51 languages. Its AI Voice Coach adds conversation practice, currently in Spanish only.


- **Who it suits:** beginners who learn by listening, and drivers
- **Free option:** 7-day trial
- **Price:** $19.99/month for one language; All Access $20.99/month (US App Store)
- **Platforms:** web, iOS, Android, Alexa
- **Note:** practice is call-and-response rather than free conversation, and the AI coach is Spanish only.


### 11. Fluently — voice tutoring for professional English


Fluently (by Fluently, Inc., also a Y Combinator company) is a voice-first AI tutor with detailed feedback on pronunciation down to individual sounds, plus work scenarios and interview practice. It now teaches 15 languages but is built around English for professionals.


- **Who it suits:** non-native English speakers preparing for work and interviews
- **Price:** not published on the site; the App Store lists several plans, monthly from $24.99
- **Platforms:** iOS, Android
- **Note:** built around English, and the website does not publish prices.


### 12. Talkio AI — AI tutors in 70+ languages and dialects


Talkio offers voice conversations with 400+ AI tutor personalities across 70+ languages and dialects, including many regional Arabic varieties, Georgian, Swahili and Basque, with word-by-word pronunciation feedback.


- **Who it suits:** learners of less common languages or specific dialects
- **Free option:** 7-day trial
- **Price:** from $14.99/month or $84.99/year (US App Store)
- **Platforms:** web, iOS, Android
- **Note:** no free tier, only a 7-day trial.


### 13. LinguaLive — realtime voice scenarios in the browser


LinguaLive is an AI voice tutor in 9 languages, built on real-time voice, with scenario practice (travel, interviews, IELTS) and corrections that don't stop the conversation. It publishes clear prices and has a usable free tier.


- **Who it suits:** learners who want scenario practice in the browser, no install
- **Free option:** 10 minutes/day in week one, then 5 minutes/day
- **Price:** $14.99/month or $99.99/year
- **Platforms:** web, iOS, Android
- **Note:** practice minutes are capped, including on Pro.


### 14. Fluently (by Engcraft) — a course plus voice role-plays, on iPhone


A different app from #11 with the same name. It pairs an A1–B2 course with goal-based AI role-play calls in 29 languages and word-by-word pronunciation scores.


- **Who it suits:** iPhone users who want course and conversation in one cheap app
- **Free option:** first 3 lessons free
- **Price:** $9.99/month or $39.99/year
- **Platforms:** iPhone, iPad, Mac
- **Note:** iPhone only.


### 15. OGIMA — speaking-first lessons plus in-person meetups


OGIMA, made in Berlin, builds lessons from real-life situations: you drill the phrases out loud with AI correction, then use them at in-person meetups with other learners in your city. No other app here connects practice to real-world events.


- **Who it suits:** intermediate learners living abroad (English, German, Spanish, Italian, French)
- **Price:** the App Store lists Premium at $17.99/month
- **Platforms:** iOS, Android
- **Note:** five languages, and the AI step is phrase drilling rather than open conversation.


### 16. Linguino — role-play lessons with an AI teacher


Linguino runs each lesson like a scene: a briefing, the 2–3 phrases you'll need, a role-play where the AI teacher plays the other person, then a replay with better ways to say things. It offers regional accents such as Mexico City or Madrid Spanish.


- **Who it suits:** beginners up to B1 who want structure inside conversation
- **Free option:** 3 short sessions a day
- **Price:** Starter $19/month
- **Platforms:** web
- **Note:** web only, and paid practice is capped by hours.


## What's the best free app for practicing speaking?


For free practice with people, **HelloTalk** and **Tandem** cost nothing, and you speak with native speakers. For free practice with an AI, **Talkpal** gives 10 minutes a day, and **Langua** and **LinguaLive** have smaller free daily allowances. Most AI tutors, ISSEN included, offer a free trial rather than a permanent free plan.


## What's the best app for a complete beginner who wants to speak?


Start with something structured. **Speak** and **Pimsleur** get beginners saying full sentences from day one, and **Linguino** builds each lesson around the phrases you'll need. Once you can hold a basic exchange, move to open conversation with an AI tutor (ISSEN, Langua, Talkpal) or a human (italki), where most speaking progress happens.


## AI tutor, human tutor, or language exchange?


- **AI tutors** (Speak, ISSEN, Praktika, Talkpal, Langua and others): available any time, no scheduling, unlimited patience, and the cheapest way to practise every day.
- **Human tutors** (italki): the best feedback and real cultural context, but the most expensive per minute and you need to book.
- **Language exchange** (HelloTalk, Tandem): free and real, but uneven; you spend half the time helping your partner.


Many learners combine them: daily AI practice, plus a human tutor or exchange partner once a week.


## Can I just use ChatGPT to practice speaking?


You can, and ChatGPT's voice mode is a decent free way to start. The difference with dedicated apps is structure: they correct you consistently, track your mistakes and level, and (in apps such as ISSEN and LinguaLive) remember what you practised last time, so each conversation builds on the previous one.


## FAQ


**What is the best app for practicing speaking a new language?** ISSEN, for open-ended conversation with an AI tutor that remembers you, on web, iOS and Android. If you want a structured course instead, Speak; for a human tutor, italki; for free practice with native speakers, HelloTalk or Tandem.


**Which app is best for conversation practice with AI?** Speak, ISSEN, Praktika, Talkpal and Langua are the strongest. See our[comparison of AI tutor apps for conversation practice](https://www.issen.com/blog/best-ai-tutor-apps-conversation-practice/) .


**How long should I practise speaking each day?** Ten to twenty minutes of out-loud practice every day does more than one long session a week.


**Are these apps available on Android and the web?** Most are on iOS and Android. italki, Tandem, ISSEN, Talkpal, Langua, Talkio and LinguaLive also run in a web browser. Fluently (by Engcraft) is iPhone only.
